seam: logos ArithmeticTheory decision vector v1 (UNFROZEN v1)
note: Language-AGNOSTIC tri-core THEORY-DECISION agreement vectors for the exact ArithmeticTheory (logos-core/arithmetic-theory@1.0.0), over two DISTINCT exact sorts: integer and decimal (#331; no float). Each entry is a ground arithmetic atom (predicate + args) together with the PINNED Theory.decide_ground outcome (#3126; the legacy decide is derived from it). The decision oracle is the Rust ArithmeticTheory in contract/rs/src/arithmetic.rs (shared by the search-side core/rs/src/builtins.rs); the Go ArithmeticTheory in contract/go/arithmetic.go and the TS one in contract/ts/src/arithmetic.ts MUST reproduce every outcome byte-for-byte. Integers route through the FROZEN ontos-data §5.1 `int` embedding (encode_int) and decimals through the FROZEN §5.9 `decimal` embedding (encode_decimal: mantissa x 10^exponent, canonical), so operand values are byte-identical across rs/go/ts BY CONSTRUCTION. int(5) and decimal(5,0) are DISTINCT terms, so `5 is 2+3.0` FAILS while `5.0 is 2+3.0` HOLDS; the comparisons (=:= < ...) order by VALUE across sorts so `2 =:= 2.0` HOLDS. Decimal `/` succeeds iff the quotient TERMINATES in base 10 (else arith_does_not_hold); `//` (truncating toward zero, result int) and `mod` (ISO floored, sign of the divisor, result decimal when an operand is decimal) are defined over decimals too (ADR 0022 Amendment), the SAME convention as the integer domain, computed exactly via integer division on scaled mantissas (no decimal `/`, so always terminating). Args are encoded structurally so each core builds the identical ontos Value: {"int": N} = the int embedding; {"bigint": "<digits>"} = the int embedding of a value beyond the JSON-int range (a string-typed INT, NOT a decimal); {"decimal": "<d.dddd>"} = the decimal embedding of that decimal literal spelling; {"atom": "<utf8>"} = a bare Atom of those bytes; {"op": "<op>", "args": [..]} = an operator compound Tuple(Atom(op), arg..); {"tuple": [..]} = a raw Tuple of the encoded children (a malformed/explicit shape); {"text": "<s>"} = the ontos-data utf8-text embedding. Since #2679 the decimal VALUE domain |exponent| <= 65536 is pinned for * and / on both sides of the bound, and the `decimal_spellings` section pins the literal parser (its own note). Outcome is "holds", {"fails": "<code>"} where the code is one of the pinned host-band sub-codes arith_does_not_hold | arith_bad_arity | arith_unknown_predicate, or (#3126) {"not_completed": "<kind>"} where the evaluator STOPPED before it decided (the kind is the stop's NonCompletionKind tag; the decimal alignment work cap is work_cap): not decided, never false, and the legacy decide answers NotMine for it. owns: is, =:=, =\=, <, >, >=, =<.

decisions.name: dec_exponent_beyond_i128_operand_fails

The structure is canonical (mantissa 1 is not divisible by 10) — only the exponent magnitude is out of band — authored as the raw tuple (decimal, int 1, bigint 10^39).

Raw tuple (decimal, int 1, bigint -10^39).

decisions.name: dec_mul_exponent_saturation_boundary
decisions.note: #475 (canonicalization exponent boundary) X is decimal(2, i128::MAX) * decimal(5, 0) -> BOTH operands decode (mantissa 2 is canonical, exponent exactly i128::MAX is in band, so from_decimal_term accepts them — distinct from #451, where the operand itself is out of band). The exponent SUM (i128::MAX + 0 = i128::MAX) is in band, so the overflow guard passes; but the product mantissa 2*5 = 10 carries ONE trailing zero, so the canonical exponent wants i128::MAX + 1 — out of the i128 scale band. rs once SATURATED the canonicalization add to i128::MAX (lowering to decimal(1, i128::MAX), wrong but encoding) while go/ts carried the increment on an unbounded big.Int/bigint (decimal(1, i128::MAX+1), which fails re-decode): a live holds/fails tri-core divergence. The fix makes the canonicalization increment CHECKED in all three from_parts, so the boundary is REJECTED identically tri-core (the * is unevaluable, the is does not hold). The i128::MAX-scale operand is authored as the raw tuple (decimal, int 2, bigint i128::MAX) — an i128::MAX-scale literal spelling is impossible (~1.7e38 fraction digits). ⚠ #1385 AMENDED: the cap at decode makes the i128::MAX-scale operand refuse at DECODE, so the sentence above about both operands decoding and the rejection happening later at canonicalization no longer describes this case. The pinned OUTCOME is unchanged (the is still does not hold) - only the refusal SITE moved earlier, and this case no longer discriminates itself from the #451 out-of-band-operand shape. Kept because the checked canonicalization it was built to pin is still the live guard for values reached through from_parts, which the ruling leaves untouched.

decisions.name: dec_div_exponent_saturation_boundary
decisions.note: #475 div twin (canonicalization exponent boundary) X is decimal(2, i128::MAX) / decimal(8, -3) -> both operands decode. div_terminating computes the quotient exponent eₐ − e_b − k where k = max(v₂(8), v₅(8)) = 3, so eₐ − e_b − k = i128::MAX − (−3) − 3 = i128::MAX (in band on a big-int), and the quotient mantissa is (2·10^3)/8 = 250, which canonicalizes to 25 at exponent i128::MAX + 1 — out of band. All three cores now REJECT, so the is does not hold; the pinned outcome is identical, only the rejection SITE differs (rs rejects earlier on the checked_sub of the raw exponent difference i128::MAX − (−3), which overflows i128; go/ts compute the difference on an unbounded big.Int/bigint and reach the checked canonicalization). Before the fix go/ts saturated/diverged here. i128::MAX-scale operand authored as the raw tuple (decimal, int 2, bigint i128::MAX). ⚠ #1385 AMENDED: same as the mul twin - the i128::MAX-scale operand now refuses at DECODE, so the per-core rejection-SITE commentary above is historical. Outcome unchanged.

decisions.name: dec_scale_bound_at_bound_decodes
decisions.note: #1385 (ruling: cap at decode) decimal(1, 65536) =:= itself -> the exponent is EXACTLY MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT, so |exponent| <= 65536 admits it and both sides decode; equal values, so the comparison HOLDS. Authored as the raw tuple (decimal, int 1, bigint 65536) because the DECODE seam is under test - a {"decimal": "..."} literal would go through the parser, whose own literal-scale cap the ruling deliberately does NOT touch. Both args identical so decodability is the only variable across this case and its three siblings.

decisions.name: dec_scale_bound_at_negative_bound_decodes
decisions.note: #1385 the negative twin: decimal(1, -65536) =:= itself -> the cap is two-sided (|exponent| <= 65536), so the lower end of the band is admitted identically and the comparison HOLDS. Pins that the bound is symmetric rather than an upper limit only.

decisions.name: dec_scale_bound_one_past_refused
decisions.note: #1385 decimal(1, 65537) =:= itself -> ONE past the bound. from_decimal_term / decFromTerm / fromTerm refuse the operand at DECODE (the existing typed refusal, no new code space), so it is not an evaluable number and the comparison does not hold. The only difference from the at-bound sibling is the exponent, so this pins the boundary itself rather than a general refusal.

decisions.name: dec_scale_bound_i128_min_refused
decisions.note: #1385 decimal(1, i128::MIN) =:= itself -> THE MEASURED DIVERGENCE VALUE, pinned so it cannot silently return: before this ruling rs ACCEPTED this exponent (its decode narrowed to i128 and i128::MIN fits) while go/ts REJECTED it (they compared |exponent| against i128::MAX, and 2^127 exceeds i128::MAX = 2^127-1). All three now refuse it at decode for the SAME reason - it is past the scale bound - so the cores agree by construction rather than by coincidence. Note the implementation must not test this with abs(): i128::MIN.abs() overflows.

decisions.name: dec_scale_gap_past_cap_add_not_decided
decisions.note: #3126 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1 -> decimal(1, 60000) and decimal(1, -60000) are both in ADR 0022's value domain (|exponent| <= 65536), and aligning them needs a shift of 120,000 > MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536): a WORK CAP, not a failure. The sum exists and exceeds 1, so the comparison holds; the evaluator stopped before it knew, so decide_ground is NotCompleted(work_cap), never Fails (until #3126 every core read the stop as arith_does_not_hold, a decided false that is untrue). The legacy decide answers NotMine for it, which every reader refuses by name.

decisions.name: dec_scale_gap_past_cap_sub_not_decided
decisions.note: #3126 10^60000 - 10^-60000 =:= 1 -> subtraction aligns the scales the same way: decimal(1, 60000) and decimal(1, -60000) are both in ADR 0022's value domain (|exponent| <= 65536), and aligning them needs a shift of 120,000 > MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536), not decided.

decisions.name: is_scale_gap_past_cap_not_decided
decisions.note: #3126 1 is 10^60000 + 10^-60000 -> is/2 evaluates its right side, which stops at the work cap: not decided, whatever the left side is.

decisions.name: dec_floordiv_scale_gap_past_cap_not_decided
decisions.note: #3126 10^60000 // 10^-60000 =:= 0 -> `//` aligns the scaled mantissas first: decimal(1, 60000) and decimal(1, -60000) are both in ADR 0022's value domain (|exponent| <= 65536), and aligning them needs a shift of 120,000 > MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536), not decided.

decisions.name: dec_mod_scale_gap_past_cap_not_decided
decisions.note: #3126 10^60000 mod 10^-60000 =:= 0 -> `mod` aligns the scaled mantissas first: decimal(1, 60000) and decimal(1, -60000) are both in ADR 0022's value domain (|exponent| <= 65536), and aligning them needs a shift of 120,000 > MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536), not decided.

decisions.name: dec_scale_gap_in_bound_control_holds
decisions.note: #3126 the control: 10^6 + 10^-6 > 1 aligns with a shift of 12, is computed, and holds.

decisions.name: cmp_stop_then_domain_error_first_stop_decides
decisions.note: #3126 (10^60000 + 10^-60000) > 1 // 0 -> the operands are evaluated left to right and the first that gives no value settles the comparison, in every core: the left operand stops at the work cap first, so the comparison is not decided.

decisions.name: cmp_domain_error_then_stop_first_stop_decides
decisions.note: #3126 (1 // 0) > 10^60000 + 10^-60000 -> the order-swapped twin: the left operand is a division by zero, a domain error, the language's answer that it has no value, so the comparison is false before the right operand is reached.

decimal_spellings.note: #2679 (seat:caa's ruling (a)): the contract's decimal-literal parser (rs BigDecimal::from_decimal_str, go decFromString, ts BigDecimal.fromString) returns through the one limit-checked constructor, so a spelling whose VALUE lies outside |exponent| <= max_exponent is refused, and 'in-band is every value the parser admits' holds by construction. Each row's spelling is prefix, then `zeros` ASCII zeros, then suffix (built by the replayer, since the strings are 65 KB). `parses` is [mantissa, exponent] (compare the decimal embedding) or null (the parser refuses). Trailing zeros are stripped before the check, so a long spelling of an in-domain value parses.
